title: What’s in the Box?
sub: PreK–Kindergarten · The Fear Boxes · Naming feelings and being brave
objective: Children will wonder what is inside a closed box, guess from sounds, and then find out that it was something harmless all along: *just a pinecone*, as the Fear Lab puts it. They will name how not knowing made them feel, notice that a heart can beat fast before anything happens, and practice a small brave step.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Feeling nervous about what we can’t see is something every brain does. Naming the feeling, and taking one small step, helps it shrink.

items.text: name a feeling we can have when we don’t know what’s coming: curious, excited, nervous or scared
items.question: name a feeling?

items.text: notice that a heart can beat fast before we even know what is in the box
items.question: say what your heart does when you don’t know?

items.text: show one small brave step: a slow breath, holding a hand, or having a look
items.question: show a brave step?

materials: A box with a lid, or a box under a cloth, with **a pinecone** inside (or another soft, harmless thing)
The *Show your class* page (page 3), projected or printed
A way to play three short sounds from the lab (the classroom screen plays them)
Crayons, including red, and the differentiated handouts
questions: What could be in the box? What else?
How does it feel not to know?
Put your hand on your heart. Is it fast or slow?
What can you do when you feel nervous?
connection: **Visit the exhibition:** the display case holds two tactile **Mystery Fear Boxes**, whose contents change every week. Let children choose: look, listen, or reach in.
**Online:** the room *What Scares You?* shows five old boxes waiting to be picked. Look at them together and guess, without opening.

steps.title: What’s in the box?
script: Sit in a circle with the covered box in the middle. Lift it and set it down gently. *“Something is in this box. What could it be?”* Take guesses. Then ask: *“How do you feel, not knowing?”* Accept every answer: curious, excited, a bit worried. Say that no one will have to touch anything today. Do not open the box yet.

screen.alt: An old striped hatbox with a rope handle, its lid shut
screen.caption: Something is in this box. What could it be?

steps.purpose: Wonder first: a closed box, and no one knows yet what is inside.
students: Look at the box. Don’t touch yet!
What could be inside? How do you feel?

steps.title: What made that sound?
script: In the Fear Lab, things pop out of the boxes. Play the three sounds one at a time and let the children guess each. Then tell them: *bubbles, a jack-in-the-box, and a feather drifting down.* All silly, and nothing scary at all.

clips.label: Sound 1
clips.credit: “Soap bubbles pop” by bojan_t95, CC0, via Freesound

screen.question: What could pop out of a box?

steps.purpose: Guess from a clue, the way the brain fills in what it cannot see.
students: What do you think made each sound?

steps.title: Just a pinecone
script: Now open your box slowly, and lift out the pinecone. Say what the Fear Lab says: our brains sometimes imagine scary things in the dark, *“when it’s really just a pinecone.”* Pass the pinecone round for anyone who wants to hold it.
steps.purpose: Find out: the thing we could not see was harmless.

steps.title: My heart goes fast
script: Ask: *“How did you feel before we opened the box?”* The Fear Lab says that when you put your hand in a box you can’t see into, *your heart races before you even touch anything.* Hands on chests. Show the feeling faces on page 3; let children point to theirs. Every feeling is allowed.

screen.question: How did you feel before we opened the box?

steps.purpose: Name the feeling, and notice the heartbeat that came with it.
students: Hand on your heart. Is it fast or slow?
Show me a curious face. A nervous face. A happy face.

steps.title: Brave steps
script: Then: *“Brave doesn’t mean never feeling scared. Brave means feeling a little scared, and taking one small step anyway.”* Practice the slowest step together: smell the flower (breathe in through the nose), blow out the candle (breathe out through the mouth), three times.

screen.text:
Slow breath.
Hold a hand.
Have a look.

steps.purpose: Give every child a small brave step to use when they feel nervous.
students: Smell the flower. Blow out the candle.

steps.title: Your handout
script: Each child works on a handout. All three show the same boxes and the same pinecone, and ask how the box made them feel.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Picture-led. Count the boxes and circle the number, follow the dots from the box to the pinecone, circle the face that shows their feeling, color the heart, trace *BRAVE*.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: A little writing. Count the boxes, draw a line from the box to the pinecone, circle a feeling, find the pinecone among harmless things, copy *BRAVE*, then draw a silly surprise.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Draw and tell. Circle a feeling and tell a grown-up why, draw what they hope is in a box, draw themselves being brave, then finish the sentence *I can be brave by…*

steps.purpose: Count, match and name feelings on paper, at the right level for each child.
students: What was in the box? Find it on your page.

steps.section: Look back and a brave breath
steps.title: Look back
script: Put the questions on the screen. For each one, the children show a thumb up, sideways or down: *“Can you now name a feeling? Can you say what your heart does when you don’t know? Can you show a brave step?”*

screen.hint: Show me: thumb up, sideways or down.

steps.purpose: Check what each child can now do against the objectives.
students: say what your heart does when you don’t know?

steps.section: Look back and a brave breath
steps.title: A brave breath
script: Close together: *“Let’s take one slow, brave breath together.”* Smell the flower, blow out the candle.

screen.question: Let’s take one slow, brave breath together.

steps.purpose: End calm, with the brave step every child can use.
